rust.error: document type declarations are not supported

reason: fast-xml-parser reads a document type declaration and expands the internal entities it declares; that reader (DocTypeReader.js with xml-naming and is-unsafe, about 400 lines) is not ported. Rust refuses the fragment, and that is the decided end state: the Open Packaging Conventions forbid DTDs in a package part. No tracked document has a DOCTYPE in a part the engine parses.

rust.error: a surrogate pair would be split

reason: fast-xml-parser takes the nine UTF-16 units after any '<![' as the CDATA opener, so a malformed opener can cut a character outside the BMP in half and leave a lone surrogate in the text. A Rust string cannot hold a lone surrogate. Rust refuses the fragment instead of inventing a replacement character.

JSZip has two UTF-8 decoders. Where a global Buffer exists (Node: CLI, tests, main process) it replaces each ill-formed sequence with U+FFFD, which is what Rust does and what the gate compares. Where none exists (a browser, and the sandboxed desktop renderer unless a bundler supplies one) it uses pako's decoder, which never rejects a byte: stray continuation bytes become control characters, a lead byte swallows the bytes after it, encoded surrogates stay lone surrogates, and the result depends on where JSZip's 16 KiB blocks end. The TypeScript engine therefore already reads ill-formed parts differently per host. Rust follows the Node behaviour everywhere. Every .xml and .rels entry of the tracked documents is well-formed UTF-8, so no tracked document is affected.

typescript.refused: zip rejected: part word/styles.xml cannot be inflated: TypeError

rust.refused: zip rejected: part word/styles.xml cannot be inflated: the deflate data is damaged or cut short

reason: The zip gate ends this message with the text of the error DecompressionStream rejects with. That text belongs to the host: Node 22 rejects with a TypeError whose message is empty, so the gate falls back to its name, and a browser words it differently. Rust writes one sentence of its own. The gate compares the message up to "cannot be inflated:", which is the part the TypeScript wrote.

rust.refused: zip rejected: part word/styles.xml cannot be inflated: bytes follow the end of the deflate data

reason: The zip gate inflates every entry through the host's DecompressionStream, and hosts differ on bytes that follow the end of a deflate stream inside an entry. Measured on 2026-11-12 with the gate's own read loop: Node 22.22.3 reads past them and the document opens; Node 26.5.0 rejects with TypeError "Trailing junk found after the end of the compressed stream"; Chromium 151.0.7922.34 (Playwright, headless) rejects with TypeError "Junk found after end of compressed data.", as the Compression Streams standard has it. The product's hosts are Chromium (the Electron renderer, the web); Electron 43 itself was not run, its Chromium is taken to do the same. Rust refuses, by the owner's decision of that day: the result of the product, not of the test host. This entry is the TypeScript loader on Node as it is. Everywhere else the gate gives the engine a DecompressionStream that rejects such bytes (host.ts), so the built and the mutated containers that have them are compared like any other. When the TypeScript gate answers alike on every host, this entry stops reproducing: then it and the stream of host.ts go. Not mirrored: where such an entry also declares less than it inflates to, Rust and host.ts name the declaration, while in Chromium the answer depends on how much output arrived before the error (64 KiB chunks; of 300,000 bytes 131,072 arrived).

latexToOmml recurses once per group and the TypeScript runs until the JavaScript stack overflows, somewhere past a thousand levels depending on the host. A stack overflow in wasm ends the instance, so Rust counts the depth and refuses past 256 levels of its reader (128 nested groups). No formula a person writes is that deep; the limit is listed because the two sides answer differently between the two limits.

A paragraph whose w:pStyle names a style the document does not have: resolveParagraphProps falls back to the default paragraph style (resolve-props.ts:493), resolveRunProps does not (line 778), so the runs lose the run properties of Normal (here italic and 20pt). Word shows them in Normal. Decided by main: the Rust falls back for runs too, and the TypeScript is to be fixed (item 12 of its list). CallSpec.listed counts the inputs of this class in resolve and fielddisplay.

drawingAnchorMeta sets noWrap when the whole fragment holds <wp:wrapNone (parse-drawing-geometry.ts:346), so the wrapNone of a drawing nested in a text box makes the square-wrapped outer anchor float in front; the comment above that line says a nested wrap must not leak. Decided by main: the Rust reads the wrap of the outer anchor only (before a:graphic), and the TypeScript is to be fixed.

attrOf of revision-xml.ts reads \s${name}="([^"]*)" only, so w:author, w:date and w:id in single quotes are absent: a filter by author, id or date never matches such a revision, and range markers pair by an empty id. Word writes double quotes, other producers do not. Decided by main: the Rust reads both quote styles, and the TypeScript is to be fixed.

vmlShapeSvg reads the opacity of a v:fill with vmlFraction, which knows a fraction and a 1/65536 count and not a percentage, so opacity="50%" is dropped and the shape is drawn opaque. Decided by main: the Rust reads the percentage (0.5), and the TypeScript is to be fixed. A negative opacity or stroke weight is written as it is on both sides.

decodeHtmlBytes and decodeMhtToHtml decode with TextDecoder, which is ICU on Node and the Encoding Standard in Chromium; the Rust uses encoding_rs, the Encoding Standard. Measured with the same bytes, Chromium 151.0.7922.34 against Node 22.22.3 (ICU 78.3): euc-kr 8C 63 gives U+B620 against U+008C c (the hangul outside KS X 1001, which Node does not read); euc-kr 81 41 gives U+AC02 against U+0081 A; shift_jis 80 gives U+0080 against U+FFFD; windows-874 DB FC gives U+FFFD U+FFFD against U+F8C1 U+F8C5; big5 87 40 gives U+43F0 against U+F266. The Rust equals Chromium on each. The product decodes in a renderer; under Node an altChunk in euc-kr with such hangul is garbled. Decided by main: the Rust stays on the Encoding Standard and the inputs are listed as differences of the Node host. CallSpec.listed counts the inputs that declare a legacy charset.

Big5 88 62 and 88 64 are the HKSCS letters the Encoding Standard decodes to two code points each (U+00CA U+0304, U+00CA U+030C). Three answers: the Rust (encoding_rs) follows the standard; Node 22.22.3 (ICU) gives one private-use character each (U+F325, U+F327); Chromium 151.0.7922.34 gives U+0093 and a lone low surrogate (U+DF04, U+DF0C), which looks like a defect of Chromium. Decided by main: the Rust follows the Encoding Standard.

The before filter of applyTrackedChangesXml goes through Date.parse, which reads a date-time without a zone as local time: the answer follows the zone of the machine (here Asia/Seoul, where 08:00 is the day before in UTC). The Rust engine has no zone and reads it as UTC. Word writes w:date with a Z. Decided by main: UTC, and the TypeScript is to read it as UTC too, which makes this entry stale. The gate itself runs in UTC (host.ts).
